name: Botswana National Museum & Art Gallery
description: The premier cultural institution of Botswana, safeguarding archaeology, natural history, ethnology and contemporary art. Complex includes National Art Gallery, Octagonal Gallery, and National Botanical Garden.
history: Built in 1967, modelled on traditional European museum practices. Closed in mid-2016 for overhaul. Recently added vintage official Daimler Limousines of Sir Seretse Khama and Sir Ketumile Masire.
collections: Permanent exhibitions on indigenous landscapes, cultural artefacts, San paintings. Octagonal Gallery: clay pots, wire toys, African masks, paintings, sculptures. National Art Gallery: traditional and contemporary African art. Natural history exhibits on Botswana biodiversity. Outdoor: historic steam locomotive, reconstructed thatched-roof houses.
additional_info: Botanical Garden hours: 07:30–16:30, Monday–Friday (except public holidays), with walking trails and flora exhibits. Offers identification service for small animals, plants, rocks, minerals.

name: Kgosi Sechele I Museum
description: A national museum housed in a former colonial police station (1902), opened to the public in 1992. A new expanded museum is under development with P60 million investment.
history: Founded in 1902, opened as museum in 1992. Housed in old colonial commissariat built by local inhabitants.
collections: Memorabilia relating to David Livingstone (1813–1873). Arts and crafts programme, educational programmes for schoolchildren, guided tours of the village. Community-based project for preservation of Kweneng culture.

name: Phuthadikobo Museum
hours: Best described as 'whenever the caretaker happens to be around'
description: A historic building of architectural interest, functioning as a museum, cultural centre, and silkscreen workshop. Unique African institution since 1975.
history: Housed in Mochudi's first school, built on a 480 sq. meter U‑plan building. Proposal approved in 1972, opened in 1975 when district council offered the abandoned Isang School building. Administered by board of trustees.
collections: Displays of local artefacts, traditional crafts, photographs. Emphasis on Bakgatla life, traditions, and design. Features a craft shop and a silkscreen printing workshop.

name: Samora Machel Museum
description: Modern museum dedicated to preserving the service and sacrifices of military personnel from various conflicts. Symbolises regional liberation solidarity.
history: Located on ground where Samora Machel stayed in 1963 on his way to join FRELIMO. Collaborative effort between Botswana and Mozambique. Gazetted as National Monument in August 2012, inaugurated in April 2022.
collections: Handwritten letters, personal diaries, photographs, documents, artefacts, military uniforms narrating Machel's life and political journey. Used for ceremonies, lectures, and veterans' events.
additional_info: Lobatse was a refuge for liberation fighters like Nelson Mandela and Oliver Tambo. Source of community pride for its humanitarian spirit.

name: Khama III Memorial Museum
address: About 800m from central shopping area on road towards Orapa
description: Museum outlining the history of the Khama dynasty, one of Southern Africa's most important royal families.
collections: Personal effects of Chief Khama III and descendants, artefacts illustrating Serowe's history. Exhibits on African insects, snakes, San culture, and temporary art displays.
additional_info: Engages local communities in narrating Bangwato history, fostering heritage preservation.

name: Supa Ngwao Museum
description: Regional Museum for Francistown and the North East Region, dedicated to human history, culture, tradition, and crafts of north east Botswana. Name means 'to show culture' in Setswana.
history: Established in 1986 as a mobile museum with aim to preserve and teach about Kalanga people and northern Botswana.
collections: Three sections: museum, information centre, craft shop. Temporary exhibitions on historic, ethnographic, and art subjects. Craft shop stocks baskets, pottery, jewellery, books. Historical artefacts include animal remains and a farm wheel.

name: Nhabe Museum
description: Museum dedicated to preserving the culture of Botswana's Northwest District. 'Nhabe' is the Bushman name for sound of cattle pulling feet through mud.
history: Opened in April 1996. Housed in a historic building built by the British military in 1939. Non-Government Organisation.
collections: Permanent displays of Ngamiland history and artefacts (musical instruments, hunting tools). Rotating exhibitions of local painters, photographers, sculptors, woodworkers, weavers. Craft shop with woven plates, bowls, trivets. Iconic basket monument at entrance.

name: Tsodilo Hills Museum
description: Small museum at the base of Tsodilo Hills explaining the archaeological and spiritual significance of over 4,500 ancient rock paintings.
collections: Cultural significance of rock paintings in a traditional Botswanan style building. Learn about archaeological discoveries and conservation efforts.

name: Livingstone Memorial Museum
description: A stone monument and museum built in 1932 near Kasane, housing some of David Livingstone's belongings.
collections: Livingstone's travelling medicine chest, Bible, and pipe.

name: Baobab Prison Tree
description: A hollow baobab tree used as a temporary jail cell in the early 20th century; also served as a post office. Now a National Monument and tourist attraction.
history: Used as jail and post office in early 1900s.

name: Kuru Museum and Cultural Centre
hours: If not open, ask around and they will open it.
description: Community-run museum and cultural centre that explains the history of the San (Basarwa) and strengthens their traditions.
history: Operated by the Kuru Development Trust; has a museum and gallery with permanent collection of art works.
collections: Art works, cultural artefacts, and exhibits on San history and culture.

name: Mokolodi Nature Reserve Museum & Education Centre
description: Museum and education centre within the nature reserve featuring a static display in a thatched hut with live snake tanks and other specimens.
collections: Snake tanks with live specimens including bugs, scorpions, beetles, and spiders.

name: Khama Rhino Sanctuary Education Centre
description: Education centre within a wildlife sanctuary, providing environmental education for children from all over Botswana.
collections: Large multi-purpose hall, two 24-bed student dormitories, accommodation for up to eight teachers.
additional_info: Primarily an education centre, not a traditional museum.

name: Kgosi Bathoen II (Segopotso) Museum
location: Mentioned in tourism guides (likely in Kanye)
description: Museum dedicated to Kgosi Bathoen II, a significant chief of the Bangwaketse.

name: National Museum Botanical Gardens
address: Part of the Botswana National Museum complex
description: Recently opened botanical gardens within the National Museum complex, featuring walking trails, labelled plants, and flora exhibits.
collections: Walking trails with labelled trees and plants, exhibits on Botswana flora, library of botanical books, historical buildings including a colonial guest house.

name: Francistown City Museum / Living Museum of Culture and Diversity
description: Francistown is positioned as a 'living museum of culture and diversity', encompassing the Supa Ngwao Museum, Domboshaba ruins, Nyangabgwe Hill, and other heritage attractions.
collections: Not a single museum; a concept covering multiple sites.

name: Kgosi Sechele I Museum (Ntsweng Site Museum)
description: A sustainable museum under construction that showcases the heritage of the area. Promises exhibitions, restaurant, camping sites, biodiversity conservation, and a state-of-the-art amphitheatre for the annual Dithubaruba Cultural Festival.
history: Under construction as an exemplary monument.
